content:
Ben Carter: dropping latest finserv messaging edits here for feedback. goal: tighten headline + proof points for regulated buyers without over-claiming. draft snippets (WIP):

1) Headline options:
A) “LLM inference for regulated workloads — fast, predictable, and auditable.”
B) “Private + dedicated LLM inference for financial services security teams can approve.”
C) “Deploy LLMs with audit logs, SSO, and customer-managed keys.”

2) Proof points bullets:
- VPC + on‑prem options (Redwood Private)
- Dedicated GPU pools w/ predictable throughput (Redwood Dedicated)
- Audit logs + export
- SSO/SAML + RBAC
- Encryption at rest + in transit; KMS/HSM integrations
- Retention/residency controls

Question: do we want to keep the line “HIPAA‑ready / HIPAA aligned” as a general regulated claim on the page? It’s in one of the earlier landing page drafts.

Soojin Lee: thx. quick reaction: finserv page shouldn’t lead w/ HIPAA anything. we can have a separate healthcare/PHI page where we’re super careful.

Soojin Lee: on headlines: A is strongest + broadest. B is good but reads salesy + “security teams can approve” is borderline (implies guaranteed approval). C is very feature-y but might work as subhead.

Camila Reyes: +1 to A as headline. we can keep “security teams can approve” for talk track maybe, but not top-of-page claim.

Ethan Wallace: I pulled “HIPAA-ready” from the regulated landing copy v0 because it tested well w/ healthcare titles, but agree it’s muddy for finserv. also worried about what Security will allow.

Naomi Feldman: pls remove “HIPAA‑ready” everywhere unless we have a very explicit qualifier. “HIPAA-ready” reads like a certification. HIPAA doesn’t certify vendors and we should not imply we’re compliant “out of the box.”

Naomi Feldman: suggested replacement language (if we need it on healthcare assets): “supports HIPAA-aligned security controls” or “can be deployed to support HIPAA-regulated workflows” — but we need to pair w/ caveat that customer config + policies matter. also: no implying we sign BAAs in hosted context unless Legal confirms.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: +1 Naomi. also please avoid “PCI compliant” / “GLBA compliant” blanket statements. approved pattern is “designed to support” + list concrete controls we provide.

Ben Carter: got it. for finserv page we’ll remove HIPAA references entirely. for regulated page, if we keep a generic line, do we say “HIPAA-aligned controls (healthcare)” in a footnote or just not mention HIPAA at all?

Soojin Lee: I’d rather not mention HIPAA on finserv/reg landing page. keep HIPAA-specific copy only on healthcare one-pager / vertical page, with Security-reviewed language.

Ethan Wallace: ok. I’ll strip HIPAA from the regulated landing draft and move the healthcare‑specific callouts into the healthcare one-pager (w/ caveats).

Tyler Benson: measurement note: if we split finserv vs healthcare landing pages, we need separate UTMs + conversion goals. if we keep single regulated page, we’ll need persona-specific sections.

Camila Reyes: we can keep one “Regulated workloads” page that’s neutral (finserv + healthcare), and then link to vertical one-pagers w/ tighter language.

Soojin Lee: on proof points bullets: please add “data isolation / customer-dedicated environment” language but be precise.

Naomi Feldman: careful w/ “data isolation” — in hosted it’s logical isolation; in Dedicated/Private we can say “single-tenant” / “customer-dedicated” depending on deployment. suggest:
- Hosted: “tenant-isolated” (no “single-tenant”)
- Dedicated: “customer-dedicated capacity”
- Private: “customer-controlled network boundary (VPC/on-prem)”

Ben Carter: makes sense. we’ll map bullets to deployment modes.

Elliot Price: also add a line about audit logs: don’t say “immutable” unless we can prove WORM storage. better: “exportable audit logs” + “integrates with customer SIEM.”

Dr. Aisha Rahman: yes. “tamper-proof” and “immutable” are no-gos unless we control the storage layer and can attest.

Ethan Wallace: proposed revised proof points (for finserv/reg page):
- Deploy in your network boundary (VPC) or on‑prem for strict data controls
- Reserved/dedicated GPU capacity for predictable throughput and SLOs
- Exportable audit logs to support investigations and governance
- SSO/SAML + role-based access controls
- Encryption in transit + at rest; supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)
- Configurable retention and regional deployment options (where available)

Thoughts?

Soojin Lee: this is close. tweak “regional deployment options” -> “regional deployment options (by region availability)” so we don’t imply everywhere.

Naomi Feldman: and tweak “supports customer-managed keys” to “supports integration with customer-managed keys via KMS (and HSM where applicable)” (keep “where applicable” so we don’t over-promise).

Ben Carter: ack. will incorporate. headline decision: A as primary; C as subhead?

Camila Reyes: yes. A headline; subhead could be: “Dedicated and private deployments with audit logs, SSO/SAML, and cost/latency controls.”

Soojin Lee: +1. also add 1-2 proof points that aren’t pure security (finserv cares about reliability/cost):
- “predictable latency under load”
- “graceful fallback / multi-region routing” (but careful: only if we can do that in the target deployment)

Ethan Wallace: for finserv one-pager we can say “routing/fallback policies available” and caveat “depends on deployment + model.”

Dr. Aisha Rahman: if you mention “multi-region,” keep it as “regional deployment options” and avoid promising “active-active” unless we actually deliver that. same for “data residency guaranteed” — say “can support data residency requirements via region selection / private deployment.”

Ben Carter: noted. I’ll keep it to “regional deployment options” + “private deployment for residency needs.”

Tyler Benson: once copy is finalized, pls tag me w/ final CTA so we can set tracking. earlier thread had CTA as “Book a security review call” vs “Download benchmark.”

Soojin Lee: CTA for regulated should be “Request a security + architecture review” (better than generic demo). benchmark download can be secondary.

Camila Reyes: agree. primary CTA = security/arch review; secondary = “Get the regulated evidence pack index” (if gated) or “View security FAQ.”

Naomi Feldman: security note: evidence pack index is ok public, but actual artifacts (SOC2 report etc.) must stay behind NDA / controlled sharing. language should reflect that.

Elliot Price: I’ll add a docs footnote: “Certain security artifacts available under NDA.”

Ben Carter: summarizing decisions:
- Remove all “HIPAA-ready” language from finserv + general regulated landing page
- Headline = “LLM inference for regulated workloads — fast, predictable, and auditable.”
- Subhead = feature/security combo (Dedicated/Private)
- Proof points updated w/ exportable audit logs wording + KMS/HSM “where applicable”
- Avoid “immutable/tamper-proof,” avoid blanket compliance statements
- CTA = request security + architecture review; secondary = security FAQ / evidence pack index (NDA caveat)

If anyone objects, speak now.

Soojin Lee: looks good. :thumbsup:

Camila Reyes: :thumbsup:

Naomi Feldman: :thumbsup: pls route final copy through Security review checklist before publish.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: +1. and pls paste final “approved language” into the messaging matrix so Sales doesn’t freestyle.

Ben Carter: will do. Ethan, can you push the edits into the Drive draft + tag Elliot for docs PR?

Ethan Wallace: on it. will update the finserv messaging framework + landing copy draft today.

Elliot Price: ping me when ready; I’ll make sure cross-links to Security FAQ + evidence pack index are consistent.
